title: Validated optimization and fitting
objective: Implement and qualify the ordinary-Python fallback slice for scalar and multivariate optimization, nonlinear systems, least squares, and fitting

oracles: SciPy differential corpus, first-order/KKT checks and independent residual validation

handoff.summary: Hardened the Linux x64 ordinary-Python fallback with exact method envelopes, independent KKT and least-squares validation, stationary-maximum rejection, callback/budget propagation, residual/data/Jacobian ceilings, scale-aware conditioning diagnostics, truthful summary traces and animations, a 31-case fail-closed portable corpus, 7 SciPy differentials, and matched CPython/Sage.js performance receipts at a7c7f797bb739058b8db92db9050c4da73ddaa6b.
risks: architecture:check stops at the integration-owned package graph because src/lib/sagejs/numerics/optimization/__init__.py has no package owner; no later architecture gate was reached in this lane.

The optimization code emits maximum_elapsed_time, but this branch intentionally depends on the integration lane's shared diagnostic-registry addition before a public timeout path can be exercised end to end.
Only Linux x64 CPython and Sage.js Node are qualified; Linux ARM64, Windows x64, macOS ARM64, browser, SEA, and four-platform release claims remain unproven.

The checked-in performance receipt confirms the translated dynamic fallback is substantially slower than CPython, especially for full iteration traces; it is correctness fallback evidence, not the planned compiled P3 performance tier.
cminpack lmdif/lmder, NLopt/PRIMA Nelder-Mead and COBYLA, nonlinear constraints, Powell, CG, Newton-CG, TNC, L-BFGS-B, and Sage find_fit compatibility remain absent and explicitly unsupported.
next_steps: Central integration: register the package owner and public numerical surface, add the package to strict Pyright configuration, merge the shared maximum_elapsed_time diagnostic, add its end-to-end timeout regression, rerun architecture:check, and then advance this task to review.

Build and qualify the universal callback-capable Wasm portfolio method by method: cminpack lmdif/lmder for Sage find_fit semantics and the permissive NLopt/PRIMA subset for Nelder-Mead/COBYLA with independent feasibility gates.
Collect browser, SEA, Linux ARM64, macOS ARM64, and Windows x64 correctness, upstream-suite, payload, memory, and performance receipts before changing any platform qualification claim.
Expand the oracle corpus with More-Garbow-Hillstrom, CUTEst subsets, badly scaled and inconsistent constraints, and dimensions crossing dense and limited-memory regimes.
